title: Progressive hysteresis circuit + tenant-priority shedding for downstream deps
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: We see correlated tail latency and error spikes in Redis and Kafka during regional bursts. Current circuit breaker behavior flips quickly and then thrashes between open/closed, causing client retries and SLO violations. Connection pools exhaust under sustained pressure and tenants with high qps cause noisy-neighbor degradations. Goal: implement a progressive 'hysteresis' circuit pattern with staged degradation, tenant-priority shedding, and region-aware failover rules so that we maintain SLOs for high-priority tenants and reduce overall error amplification.
background_and_context: Related observations from telemetry: (1) Redis p99 spikes correlate with sudden increases in multi-tenant cache miss storms; (2) Kafka producer backpressure cascades to request timeouts, then to retries; (3) SQL connection pools reach max and block foreground requests. Existing circuits are binary; we need graded states (Closed -> Strained -> Soft-Open -> Open) with configurable dwell times and progressive shedding. This ticket complements conn-slimming work (ENG-301234) and regional governor spillover patterns (ENG-462311).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Circuit state machine implemented with at least four states and tunable hysteresis timers per-region and per-dependency.
2) Tenant-priority lanes exist: high, normal, background. Admission respects lanes; background can be probabilistically shed based on dynamic thresholds.
3) Connection pool admission implements 'soft-reserve' for high-priority tenants preventing starvation.
4) Rollout has canary and global switch; metrics show reduced p99 for high-priority tenants during synthetic overload by >=30% without increasing p50 significantly.
5) Playbook entries and runbook steps added to Console for on-call operations.
6) End-to-end integration tests and chaos test harness exercise state transitions and shedding behavior.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 - Library: Implement hysteresis CB library (state machine + backoff windows) and per-tenant scoring.
Phase 2 - Runtime integration: Wire into Redis/Kafka/DB dependency proxies and connection pool admission. Expose policy config via config store and Console UI toggles.
Phase 3 - Telemetry: Add detailed state transition events, tenant-level drop counters, and SLO burn-down dashboards.
Phase 4 - Canary & Rollout: Canary in eu-west-1 for non-critical tenants, run synthetic spike tests, iterate thresholds.
Phase 5 - Global: Promote across regions and add automated fallback to compatible model variants where applicable.
design_notes_and_tradeoffs:
- We prefer staged degradation (soft-open) to avoid oscillation. Dwell timers reduce flapping but add time-to-recover; we'll make them configurable per-customer SLA.
- Probabilistic shedding reduces cliff-drop transients but may affect fairness; we will prioritize tenants by SLA weight and track effective throughput.
- Soft-reserve reduces available capacity for normal tenants; to mitigate, soft-reserve is bounded by fractional capacity and reclaims unused reservations after idle timeout.
- Avoid heavy control-plane churn: policy updates are rate-limited and validated by canary before global apply.
- Complexity tradeoff: we add instrumentation to debug state transitions with unique trace ids to correlate across subsystems.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for state machine and timer behaviors.
- Integration tests: simulate connection pool exhaustion and verify admission and soft-reserve enforcement.
- Chaos engineering: inject elevated latency and error rates into Redis/Kafka replicas, assert graceful degradation and stable state transitions.
- Benchmark: measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 and error rates under ramped load for high vs normal tenants.
- Regression: run existing conn-slimming tests (ENG-301234) to ensure compatibility.
observability_checklist:
- New metrics: cb_state_{dep,region,tenant}, cb_transition_count, tenant_shed_count, tenant_soft_reserve_in_use, connpool_wait_time_by_tier.
- Logging: structured events for each transition with reason, threshold, and trace id.
- Dashboards: SLO burn-down by tenant and region, heatmap of shedding by dependency.
- Alerts: SLO-breach alert when high-priority tenants have error rate > threshold for 5m.
- Audit: config-change audit trail in Console.
runbook_and_rollout:
- Start with feature flag off. Canary in eu-west-1 for 2% of traffic (non-critical tenants) for 48h with synthetic spike.
- If canary passes thresholds, expand to 10% then 50% with progressive knob adjustments.
- Fast rollback via Console flag.
- On-call steps: 1) disable shedding, 2) increase soft-reserve for high-priority lanes, 3) trigger regional failover if dependency region degraded.
- Postmortem: capture transition logs and adjust hysteresis intervals if needed.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: misconfigured thresholds cause over-shedding; Mitigation: safe defaults and per-tenant dry-run mode.
- Risk: added latency from admission path; Mitigation: optimize hot path and benchmark, keep decision logic O(1).
- Risk: tenant isolation imperfect under extreme pressure; Mitigation: conservative soft-reserve budgeting and burst credits.
- Risk: increased operational complexity; Mitigation: invest in dashboards, runbooks, and training.
